_notes: clinical_key is null when this species has no entry in A-M2's severity/antivenom engine — Snake ID must still identify it, but must NOT claim a clinical severity assessment for it. medical_significance is independent of clinical_key: a species can be genuinely venomous/dangerous (King Cobra) without A-M2 having a bite-symptom model for it.

Spectacled_Cobra.note: Big Four species — bite symptoms map directly to A-M2's clinical model.

Monocled_Cobra.note: Approximated to A-M2's generic cobra entry — same genus, similar neurotoxic venom, but treat this mapping as a clinical approximation, not an exact match.

Saw_scaled_Viper.note: Big Four species — direct clinical match.

Russells_Viper.note: Big Four species — direct clinical match.

Common_Krait.note: Big Four species — direct clinical match.

King_Cobra.note: Genuinely dangerous neurotoxic venom, but a different genus from A-M2's cobra model — no direct clinical mapping exists. Show identification + general danger warning only; do not route into A-M2 severity scoring.

Checkered_Keelback.note: Mildly rear-fanged, not medically significant for humans in almost all cases. Still advise standard bite hygiene, not a 'safe, ignore it' message.

Common_Rat_Snake.note: Non-venomous constrictor, commonly mistaken for a cobra by frightened bystanders — worth calling that out explicitly in the UI copy.

Indian_Rock_Python.note: Non-venomous constrictor. Bite risk is mechanical (crush/laceration), not toxinological.

Green_Tree_Vine.note: Mildly rear-fanged (Ahaetulla). Bites are very rarely medically significant, but avoid a blanket 'harmless' claim — advise standard wound care and monitoring.
